thread.title: Coherent (NASDAQ: COHR ) is trading at less than $270 per sh

author: Joel Harris
title: Coherent (NASDAQ: COHR ) is trading at less than $270 per sh
text:
Coherent (NASDAQ: COHR ) is trading at less than $270 per share, down nearly 20% in the last 10 days after news of disappointing iPhone X sales and rumors of discontinuation. The entire OLED market has dropped on this news, with OLED manufacturer Universal Display Corp.’s (NASDAQ: OLED ) value taking a similar hit (down 18% since January 17).
I believe that this won’t impact Coherent’s long-term valuation, and this market overreaction makes a great buying opportunity.
COHR data by YCharts 
Why Coherent's valuation shouldn’t be affected: There are still myriad smartphone OEMs incorporating OLEDs into their high-end smartphones. Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ) has been using them for a while and will continue to do so in the upcoming Galaxy S9. Chinese OEMs (such as Huawei, Vivo) are incorporating them in their 2018 models. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) will not be left in the dust on OLED technology, as they have built a reputation as a premium brand. I don’t think they will let other, ‘cheaper’ phone OEMs surpass them in screen quality. OLEDs will also be forced upon Apple before long, especially if they want curved displays or other unique features that are easier to implement with OLED displays.
In addition to this, Apple is likely desperate to find an OLED supplier other than their main competitor, Samsung. There is great incentive for manufacturers to start volume production of OLEDs to win Apple contracts, which will likely involve making upwards of 50 million displays annually. The role of excimer laser annealing in processing LTPS backplates can’t be circumvented, and Coherent’s excimer lasers will play a role in the upscaling of these manufacturers.
